ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.2m. It is bronze-brown above with a distinct black lateral stripe and a pale yellow-green venter. It features a prominent white neck stripe and large, dark-rimmed eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish the Common Bronzeback by the distinct, thin black stripe running horizontally through its eye, which separates the bronze upper body from the pale belly.
ai.habitat: The Common Bronzeback inhabits lowland forests, plantations, and gardens, typically found in vegetation up to 1,000 meters in altitude across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Common Bronzeback is a diurnal, agile hunter that actively pursues lizards and frogs through vegetation, often using its speed to escape when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis pictus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, often between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Common Bronzeback occurs across Northeast India, the Western Ghats, and the Eastern Himalayas, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
